# pipelino

> A staged pipeline for async work in the browser and Node: per-stage concurrency, batching by count and weight, pause and cancel, live progress. Zero dependencies, 2.6 KB gzipped. ESM only; runs in current browsers, Node 18+, Deno and Bun.

Install with `npm install pipelino`.

```ts
import { createPipeline } from 'pipelino';

const pipeline = createPipeline<Photo>({
  stages: [
    { name: 'inspect', concurrency: 8, run: async (photo) => ({ width: await readWidth(photo.file) }) },
    { name: 'thumbnail', concurrency: 4, run: async (photo) => ({ thumb: await makeThumb(photo.file) }) },
    {
      name: 'upload',
      barrier: true, // start only once every photo has its thumbnail
      batch: { size: 10 },
      runBatch: (photos, { signal }) => upload(photos, signal),
    },
  ],
});

pipeline.on('progress', ({ overall }) => render(overall.percent));
pipeline.on('done', ({ done, failed }) => console.log(done.length, failed.length));
pipeline.push(photos); // any objects with a unique string `id`
```

- Every item needs a unique string `id`; `push()` throws for an item without one.
- A stage returns an object whose fields are merged into the item, or nothing. A string, array or number fails the item.
- A batch stage uses `batch` with `runBatch(items, ctx)` and returns one patch per item in the same order, or nothing.
- Pass `ctx.signal` to `fetch` and workers so `cancel()` stops work that is in flight.
- A stage that throws fails only that item: it skips the remaining stages and is listed in `done.failed`. Nothing is retried; push a failed item again to re-run it.
- `on()` returns the unsubscribe function; there is no `off()`.
